name: english-and-british-monarchs

description.en: The 42 monarchs of England from William I (1066), of Great Britain from 1707 and of the United Kingdom from 1801, to Charles III. Front: the monarch's regnal name in English and Swedish; back: the years of the reign, counted from accession rather than coronation, with both periods for the two kings who reigned twice (a single year means the whole reign fell within that year); a note gives the royal house. Disputed claimants (Empress Matilda, Lady Jane Grey) are not counted, William III and Mary II have a card each, and there was no monarch during the Interregnum of 1649–1660. Based on Wikidata and the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (public domain), and checked against the Royal Household's website (royal.uk) and Wikipedia.
description.sv: De 42 monarkerna i England från Vilhelm I (1066), i Storbritannien från 1707 och i Förenade kungariket från 1801, fram till Charles III. Framsida: monarkens regentnamn på engelska och svenska; baksida: regeringsåren, räknade från trontillträdet och inte från kröningen, med båda perioderna för de två kungar som regerade två gånger (ett enda årtal betyder att hela regeringstiden föll inom det året); en anteckning anger kungahuset. Omstridda tronpretendenter (kejsarinnan Matilda, Jane Grey) räknas inte, Vilhelm III och Maria II har ett kort var, och under interregnumet 1649–1660 fanns ingen monark. Uppgifterna bygger på Wikidata och 1911 års upplaga av Encyclopædia Britannica (fri från upphovsrätt) och är kontrollerade mot det brittiska kungahusets webbplats (royal.uk) och Wikipedia.

method: Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with independent AI reviewers and machine checks (the builder's checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert. Every query, URL and command run is listed under queries; the raw responses were saved in the research scratch directory.

Offices: the Wikidata API (query 1) found the four items for the offices the deck covers: Monarch of England (Q18810062), Monarch of Great Britain (Q110324075, 1707–1800), monarch of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (Q111722535, 1801–1927) and Monarch of the United Kingdom (Q9134365, since 1927).

Selection and reign years: query 2 listed every non-deprecated position-held (P39) statement for the four offices with its start and end times. The query's filter, a start time in 1066 or later (FILTER(YEAR(?start) >= 1066)), returns 44 people: Harold Godwinson (Q159597), whose statement starts on 6 January 1066 (Julian; the endpoint shows 1066-01-11 after converting to Gregorian), and the 43 holders whose first statement starts on or after William I's accession on 25 December 1066 (Julian). Harold, the last king before the Norman Conquest, was then removed by hand, because the deck starts with the Norman Conquest; the Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings before him are already outside the filter. That left 43 people. Lady Jane Grey (Q162356), who has a P39 statement for July 1553, was left out as a disputed claimant (see the selection), leaving 42 cards. The statements of one person under successive offices were joined into one reign (Anne: England 1702–1707 and Great Britain 1707–1714; George III: Great Britain 1760–1801 and the United Kingdom 1801–1820; George V: 1910–1927 and 1927–1936). Reigns interrupted by another monarch keep both periods (Henry VI, Edward IV). The back gives the years only, start–end with an en dash; a reign that began and ended in the same year is a single year (Edward V, Edward VIII), and the description says so, since in the back-to-front direction "1483" and "1936" are years in which other monarchs also reigned; the reigning monarch's back is open-ended ("2022–").

Calendar: Wikidata stores most dates before the British calendar change of 1752 in the Julian calendar (calendar model Q1985786), and the SPARQL endpoint (queries 2 and 23) returns every date converted to the proleptic Gregorian calendar, e.g. William I's start time, stored as 25 December 1066 (Julian), comes back as 1066-12-31. The first version of the dossier quoted the converted dates; in quality-control round 4 every date in the cards' Wikidata evidence was replaced by the value as stored, with its calendar model (Julian or Gregorian), from a fresh wbgetentities download (query 20). No year on any card changes. Some of Wikidata's dates around 1700 are stored as Gregorian although they are the Old Style days (e.g. William III, 28 December 1694); they are quoted as stored.

Reign convention: a reign is counted from accession, the moment the previous monarch died, abdicated or was deposed (the Royal Household's accession page: "A new Sovereign succeeds to the throne as soon as his or her predecessor dies"), not from coronation; so Edward V and Edward VIII, who were never crowned, are counted. The convention changes the start year of many reigns (Elizabeth II, for example, acceded on 6 February 1952 and was crowned in 1953); for William I, who came to the throne by conquest, Wikidata's statement starts on 25 December 1066 (Julian), the day of his coronation (the 1911 Britannica), so the year is 1066 either way. Charles II's reign is given from the Restoration in 1660, as Wikidata does (start time 29 May 1660, Julian) and the Royal Household and Wikipedia confirm, with a note that he had taken the title of king on his father's execution in 1649 (the 1911 Britannica).

Names: the English front is the regnal name: the Wikidata English or multilingual ("mul") label or alias of the person, or that label with the territorial suffix ("of England", "of Great Britain") removed (query 4; e.g. the mul label "Henry VIII", the en label "John of England" shortened to "John"); the Royal Household's page headings and the English Wikipedia lists write the names the same way (verification). The Swedish front is the established Swedish form: the Wikidata Swedish label or alias with the territorial suffix ("av England", "av Storbritannien") removed, e.g. "Henrik VIII av England" (with the alias "Henrik VIII"), "Vilhelm I av England" (alias), "Johan av England", "Stefan av Blois", "Anna av Storbritannien", "Viktoria av Storbritannien". The Swedish forms translate the given name as Swedish has long done for historical monarchs (Vilhelm, Henrik, Rikard, Johan, Edvard, Maria, Elisabet, Jakob, Karl, Anna, Georg, Viktoria) but keep "Elizabeth II" and "Charles III" untranslated: that is how the Wikidata Swedish labels and the Swedish Wikipedia articles write them ("Elizabeth II av Storbritannien", "Charles III av Storbritannien"). Each Swedish form was checked against the first sentence of the person's Swedish Wikipedia article (query 13), which is quoted in the card's evidence. Nationalencyklopedin and Språkrådet could not be read from the research environment (query 15).

Royal houses (the back note): the house is the Wikidata P53 (family) of the monarch (query 3), named by the house item's English label and, in Swedish, its Swedish label (query 5: Normandiska ätten, Huset Plantagenet, Huset Lancaster, Huset York, Huset Tudor, Huset Stuart, Huset Nassau-Oranien, Huset Hannover, Huset Windsor). For James I, Charles II, James II, Mary II and Anne Wikidata's P53 is Q3973466 "House of Stewart di Darnley", which Wikidata has as part of (P361) the House of Stuart (Q179840), Charles I's P53; the notes give the House of Stuart, and the builder checks both statements. Where Wikidata gives several houses (Henry II: Plantagenet, Normandy and Angevins; Henry IV: Lancaster and Plantagenet; Elizabeth II: Windsor, preferred, besides Saxe-Coburg and Gotha and the British royal family; Charles III: Windsor and Glücksburg), the note gives the one the monarch shares with the neighbouring monarchs, or the preferred one; George V's note gives both of his, with Wikidata's 1917 qualifiers. Stephen is of the House of Blois and William III of the House of Orange-Nassau (Wikidata P53). "Huset Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" is the Wikidata Swedish label "Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" (Q1753846) with "Huset" prefixed, as in the other Swedish house labels, and is also the Swedish Wikipedia's usage (the category "Huset Sachsen-Coburg-Gotha" on the article on Edvard VII). "Huset Blois" is the compiler's rendering in the same pattern (Q1590002 has no Swedish label), confirmed by Swedish Wikipedia usage (query 14). The Royal Household's house pages and the English Wikipedia lists' sections were consulted to confirm the houses (verification only). Where the Wikidata P53 value is the house the note names, the builder checks it.

Cross-check against the Royal Household: the royal.uk sitemap (query 7) gave the URLs of the history pages; the list "Kings and Queens from 1066" and the page of each monarch and house were downloaded (queries 8 and 9). The heading of each monarch's page (e.g. "Henry VI (r.1422-1461 and 1470-1471)") was compared by the dossier script with the card's back: the headings of the 39 monarch pages (William III and Mary II share one) agree with the 40 cards' years. For Elizabeth II and Charles III, which have no such heading, the accession page (6 February 1952), the news items of 8 September 2022 and the Court Circular of 1 October 2026 ("The King and Queen this evening received …") were read; the last confirms that Charles III was still reigning shortly before the deck was made.

Independent cross-check: the English Wikipedia lists of English and of British monarchs (query 10) give exact accession and end dates for every card; rows.py printed the name and reign cell of every row, and every card's years agree with them. These lists cite the Royal Household among other references, so they are not wholly independent of it; Britannica and Historic Royal Palaces, the intended independent references, refused the research environment's requests (HTTP 403, query 15). Wikidata's statements, the content source, agree with them except as recorded in quality control (William III's own statement starts in 1694, Stephen's reign is split in two, Mary I's start day).

Notes: each back note starts with the royal house and, where it helps the learner, adds a short fact in the compiler's own words. Every such fact comes from a content source: from Wikidata (nicknames as aliases, e.g. "William Rufus"/"Vilhelm Rufus", "Richard the Lionheart"/"Rikard Lejonhjärta", "John I Lackland"/"Johan utan land", "William of Orange", "James VII of Scotland"/"Jakob VII av Skottland"; P39 qualifiers for joint reigns (P1706) and abdications (P1534) and for successors; deaths (P1196, P509, P570); the items Lady Jane Grey Q162356, Empress Matilda Q150872, Magna Carta Q12519, Battle of Bosworth Field Q222013, Princes in the Tower Q648580, Interregnum Q2558636, Stuart Restoration Q846848, Glorious Revolution Q189508, Acts of Union 1707 Q193515, Regency era Q25861 and House of Windsor Q81589; the first and last monarch of a house from the P53 statements, and the longest reign from the P39 statements, query 22; James I as the first holder of both the English and the Scottish crown, query 23), or, where Wikidata does not state it, from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource (query 21; the facts are listed in that source's usedFor). Each is quoted in the card's evidence. The Royal Household and Wikipedia were consulted to confirm them and supplied none. In quality-control round 4 the facts that neither content source states were removed or reworded: Edward V and Edward VIII never crowned (removed), the Royal Household grouping William III with the Stuarts (removed), Charles II's regnal years officially counted from 1649 (now: he took the title of king in 1649), Richard I and John as Angevin kings (now: Henry II counted among the Angevins, from his father's county of Anjou), Richard II "deposed" (now: forced to give up the throne, as Wikidata's abdication and the 1911 Britannica have it) and James II "deposed" (now: lost the throne in the Glorious Revolution).
Study direction: every back is unique (the builder checks this), and asking for the monarch from the reign years makes sense, so the deck is bidirectional.

The dossier was written by a script (build_dossier.py) from the saved responses and a hand-written table of the cards (cards_data.py), so that every quoted Wikidata value, royal.uk heading and Swedish Wikipedia sentence is copied from the saved data and asserted to be verbatim; the builder then ran its Wikidata checks against live Wikidata (query 17).

Helper scripts: the research used small Python scripts in the research scratch directory, which are not published with the deck; what each did: wd.py ran Wikidata API searches, SPARQL queries (POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, retrying on HTTP 429/5xx) and entity downloads and saved the JSON responses; sitemap.py downloaded the three royal.uk sitemap pages and printed the URLs whose path names a monarch, a house or the history pages; royal.py downloaded royal.uk pages, saved the HTML and reduced the <main> element to plain text (scripts and styles removed, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed); wiki.py fetched Wikipedia articles through the MediaWiki API (revision id, wikitext and plain-text introduction); rows.py printed the section headings and the name-and-reign cell of every table row in the two English Wikipedia lists' wikitext, with references and footnote templates removed; cards_data.py is the hand-written table of the cards (fronts, backs, notes, which page and row each card's evidence quotes), and build_dossier.py assembled the dossier from it and the saved responses, asserting that every quoted value occurs verbatim in the saved data. Split P39 statements of one person were merged by hand in cards_data.py, as step 2 describes. In quality-control round 3 the name part of each card's Wikidata evidence was rewritten from a fresh wbgetentities download (query 18) by a further script, which states which label or alias the card text is, or which one it shortens. In quality-control round 4: fetch.py downloaded the full entities (wbgetentities: labels, aliases, descriptions, claims) of the 42 monarchs and of the house, office and event items; show.py printed selected statements with their qualifiers, times as stored and calendar models; search.py ran wbsearchentities and label lookups; ws.py fetched 1911 Britannica articles from Wikisource (parse API: revision id and rendered text, tags stripped) and grep.py printed passages from them; patch4.py rewrote the dossier, asserting that every 1911 Britannica quotation occurs verbatim in the saved text and generating the Wikidata dates from the saved entities.
selection: All monarchs of England from William I (1066) to the union with Scotland, of Great Britain from 1707 and of the United Kingdom from 1801 to the present, Charles III: the holders of the four Wikidata offices from 1066, 42 people with a card each. The deck starts at 1066 because the brief is the post-Conquest monarchy (the Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, Harold Godwinson and Edgar Ætheling are left out). Left out as disputed claimants, whom the English Wikipedia lists under "Disputed claimant": Empress Matilda (in 1141; the Royal Household treats her with Stephen, 1135–1154, and Wikidata has no office statement for her), Louis of France (1216–1217) and Lady Jane Grey (proclaimed 10 July 1553, deposed 19 July; the Royal Household lists her, "Lady Jane Grey (r. 10-19 July 1553)", and says "six if Lady Jane Grey is included" of the Tudors, Wikidata has an office statement for her, but the English Wikipedia lists her as a disputed claimant, and her nine days are not counted as a reign in this deck): she is mentioned in the note on Mary I. William III and Mary II, joint monarchs from 1689, have a card each with their own years (1689–1702 and 1689–1694), as the Royal Household gives them. The Interregnum (1649–1660, the Commonwealth and the Protectorate of Oliver and Richard Cromwell) had no monarch and has no card; it is mentioned in the notes on Charles I and Charles II. Edward V (1483) and Edward VIII (1936), who reigned but were never crowned, are included, since a reign is counted from accession. The monarchs of Scotland before 1603 and of Ireland are not included, except as the same people (James I, also James VI of Scotland). Charles III's reign is open-ended, as of 4 October 2026.

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's reign against Wikidata's P39 statements, the Royal Household's page headings and the English Wikipedia lists; the Swedish names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; the houses against the Royal Household's house pages, Wikidata P53 and the English Wikipedia; the contested cases.
rounds.scope: All 42 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: The Royal Household's headings and the English Wikipedia lists agree on the years of all 42 reigns, and the Swedish Wikipedia introductions agree wherever they give the years; Wikidata agrees except for William III's start (1694 for 1689) and the split of Stephen's reign, where the cards follow the better sources and no check depends on the Wikidata value. The contested cases were decided as the selection explains (Matilda, Louis and Lady Jane Grey left out; William III and Mary II a card each; no card for the Interregnum; Edward V and Edward VIII counted from accession). The brief's Swedish "Karl III" was replaced by the established "Charles III". Builder checks cover every front in both languages, every office and most houses.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P39 (Monarch of England) statement for William III starts on 28 December 1694 (stored as Gregorian), the day Mary II died, i.e. at the start of his sole reign; the Royal Household ("William III (r. 1689-1702) and Mary II (r. 1689-1694)"), the English Wikipedia list (13 February 1689 – 8 March 1702) and the Swedish Wikipedia all date his reign from 1689.
findings.resolution: Back 1689–1702, following the better sources; the note says he reigned jointly with Mary II until 1694. The builder checks only that he held the office (P39), not the start year; the discrepancy is recorded in the card's evidence.

findings.issue: Wikidata has two P39 statements for Stephen, 22 December 1135 (Julian) – April 1141 and November 1141 – 25 October 1154 (Julian), as stored, leaving out his captivity in 1141; the Royal Household gives one reign, "Stephen and Matilda (r. 1135-1154)", and the English Wikipedia list 22 December 1135 – 25 October 1154, with Matilda as a disputed claimant in 1141.
findings.resolution: Back 1135–1154, one reign, as the Royal Household and Wikipedia give it; the note says Matilda fought him for the throne but is not counted. Recorded in the card's evidence.

findings.issue: Wikidata starts Mary I's reign on 29 July 1553 (Julian, as stored) (after Lady Jane Grey's P39 statement, 10–19 July 1553, Julian); the English Wikipedia list starts it on 19 July 1553 and the Swedish Wikipedia "från den 19 juli 1553". The Royal Household gives the year only.
findings.resolution: The card gives years only, 1553–1558, on which all sources agree; Lady Jane Grey is left out (selection) and mentioned in the note.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P39 start time for William I is 25 December 1066 (Julian, as stored), the day of his coronation, which is also where the English Wikipedia list dates his reign from (after the Battle of Hastings). (Corrected in round 4: this finding first quoted the SPARQL endpoint's Gregorian conversion, 1066-12-31, as if Wikidata disagreed.)
findings.resolution: No discrepancy; the year is 1066 by any convention, and the note gives the coronation on Christmas Day 1066.

findings.issue: Lady Jane Grey has a Wikidata P39 statement (10–19 July 1553, Julian, as stored) and a Royal Household page ("Lady Jane Grey (r. 10-19 July 1553)"), so a mechanical selection would include her; the English Wikipedia lists her as a disputed claimant.
findings.resolution: Left out with Matilda and Louis as a disputed claimant, a decision explained in the selection and stated in the description; she is named in the note on Mary I so the learner knows of her.

findings.issue: Wikidata models Anne, George III and George V with two P39 statements each, for the successive offices (England then Great Britain; Great Britain then the United Kingdom; the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland then the United Kingdom).
